# Dependencies Report

`mxcli report dependencies` lists what the app stands on and whether it is current and
safe. It reads the project and asks two online sources — the Marketplace (with a token)
and the OSV advisory database — and says per item what it could not check.

## Run it

```bash
mxcli auth login                                   # once: lets it compare with the Marketplace
mxcli report dependencies -p app.mpr -o docs/dependencies.html
mxcli report dependencies -p app.mpr --format json -o deps.json
mxcli report dependencies -p app.mpr --offline     # no network at all
```

## Reading it

- **High or critical vulnerabilities** lead the page. Upgrade the jar to the version in
  "Upgrade to at least" — the lowest fix above the installed version for every advisory
  that names one. When an advisory does not apply (the vulnerable class or feature is
  not used), record why instead of ignoring it:

  ```yaml
  items:
    "vuln:GHSA-4w82-r329-3q67": {status: accepted, note: "no polymorphic typing; ObjectMapper is never configured with default typing"}
  ```

  Pass it with `--annotations`; the verdict then leaves it out of the count.
- **A jar "not checked"** has no `META-INF/maven/…/pom.properties`, so it has no
  Maven coordinates to look up — often a hand-built jar. Find its source and version
  by hand, or replace it with a published artifact.
- **Marketplace modules** are matched by the version UUID they record, so "newer
  available" is certain. "Not identified" with "withdrawn" means the Marketplace no
  longer publishes the installed version: plan the move to the version it names.
  **Before updating**, run `mxcli marketplace diff <content-id> -p app.mpr` — an update
  replaces the module and drops local changes.
- **Widgets** are matched by name only (a widget package records no Marketplace ID).
  Widgets that ship inside a module (the Datagrid filters in Data Widgets) have no
  catalog entry of their own. After updating widgets, `mxcli report` shows CE0463 under
  Builds until `mxcli fix widgets` updates the pages.
- **Release line**: a monthly release is supported only until the next one; plan the
  move to an LTS or MTS version. mxcli knows the lines, not the support end dates.

## What it does not cover

JavaScript dependencies inside widgets, the Mendix runtime itself, and whether the
app actually reaches the vulnerable code.
